report.releaseDate: 10 Nov 2026 (preliminary Q3/9M announcement, Euronext Athens) / 20 Nov 2026 (full 9M 2026 press release, slides and call)
report.currency: EUR (tables in € millions; ~USD equivalents at EUR/USD 1.10)
report.verdict: Operationally a clean quarter inside a stretched balance sheet: UK online NGR grew 12.2% cc through the first full quarters of 40% RGD, group AEBITDA edged up 5% QoQ to €88.9m (~$98m) at a 31.1% margin, and the legacy lottery business stabilised QoQ. But pro-forma net leverage climbed to 4.33x (vs 3.5x at Dec-25 and a 4.75x covenant) because the LTM denominator is shrinking, the evoke close has slipped into 2027, and the group still reported a €23.8m (~$26m) Q3 net loss after €40.1m (~$44m) of finance costs and €13.7m (~$15m) of deal fees. Deleveraging now depends on Q4 seasonality and a US jackpot cycle, neither of which management controls.
summary: **Headline: revenue €286.1m (~$315m), +249% YoY and +3.6% QoQ; AEBITDA €88.9m (~$98m), +197% YoY and +5.1% QoQ.** The YoY optics are meaningless (Bally's International Interactive, 'BII', was only consolidated from Q4-25); the relevant read is sequential: AEBITDA +€4.3m (~$5m) QoQ with margin +50bps to 31.1%. There is no published sell-side consensus for INLOT; the parent Bally's Corp printed Q3 revenue of $807.6m vs a $807.85m estimate (in line).

**9M 2026: revenue €830.3m (~$913m) vs €263.9m; AEBITDA €273.6m (~$301m) vs €90.1m; margin 33.0% vs 34.2%.** On a pro-forma basis (as if BII owned throughout) management disclosed 9M AEBITDA down ~15% YoY — i.e. the combined group lost roughly €48m (~$53m) of EBITDA YoY, essentially the UK duty hit plus US lottery weakness.

**No formal numeric guidance exists and none was introduced.** Bally's Intralot gives qualitative direction only: continued UK online growth, a stronger H2 in US lottery and Turkey (H1 call), and evoke completion now 'in 2027' (Earnings+More cites January 2027). The 'guidance bridge' for this name is therefore the LTM pro-forma AEBITDA that drives the leverage covenant: €430.8m (~$474m) at Dec-25 → €376.7m (~$414m) at Sep-26.

**The division that drove the quarter was BII (B2C online), +4.0% QoQ to €201.6m (~$222m), 70% of group revenue.** UK online revenue rose 3.8% QoQ (+€6.8m) and 12.2% YoY in constant currency, a third straight quarter of acceleration (10.5% → 11.6% → 12.2%) and a third consecutive all-time-high quarterly NGR — achieved on lower marketing spend. Spain hit a record €13.3m (~$15m), +18.9% YoY on a larger active base.

**UK Remote Gaming Duty (21% → 40% from 1 Apr 2026) cost ~€34m (~$37m) of gross AEBITDA in Q3, in line with Q2; 9M gross hit ~€68m (~$75m).** Management says ~55% of the Q3 hit was offset YoY (Q2: 65%) via top-line growth, marketing efficiency and cost control. Note the metric is loosely defined: the 9M components disclosed (gross-profit growth €26.2m + fixed-cost actions €6.8m = €33.0m) equal ~49% of €68m, consistent with iGB's 'nearly half' rather than 55-65%. Gaming-tax expense in the P&L was €76.8m (~$84m) in Q3 and €192.2m (~$211m) for 9M.

**Legacy Intralot (B2B lottery + Bilyoner/Argentina) revenue was €84.5m (~$93m) in Q3, +2.7% QoQ and +3.2% YoY vs the €81.9m Q3-25 standalone base; AEBITDA €26.0m (~$29m), +6.3% QoQ but -13% YoY (Q3-25: €29.9m).** The QoQ improvement was Bilyoner (+€4.7m AEBITDA) and Argentina; B2B went the other way.

**B2B lottery remains the soft spot: 9M revenue €191.0m (~$210m), -8.1% reported / -6.2% cc.** The US, the largest market, fell 11% cc to €119.6m (~$132m) against a prior year flattered by record jackpots and on lower equipment sales; the rest of the B2B portfolio grew 3.6% cc. Management keeps framing this as jackpot cyclicality and seasonality; the equipment-sales shortfall is less cyclical.

**Legacy B2C (Bilyoner Turkey + Argentina) 9M revenue €60.1m (~$66m), +7.1%.** Bilyoner grew 20.6% in local currency but only 3.4% in euros to €45.8m (~$50m) — TRY depreciation ate most of it — with amounts wagered +28.4% vs a market +17.8% (share gain). Q3 Bilyoner revenue rebounded 25.8% QoQ (+€3.3m) after a seasonal Q2 drop of 21.8%. Argentina grew 21.1% to €14.3m (~$16m) for 9M.

**Below AEBITDA the P&L is heavy: Q3 D&A €45.2m (~$50m), net finance costs €40.1m (~$44m), transaction fees €13.7m (~$15m) → pre-tax loss €14.3m, net loss after tax €23.8m (~$26m), NIATMI €(26.6)m.** 9M: finance costs €109.7m (~$121m, vs €20.5m), D&A €130.7m, deal fees €27.7m (~$30m), net loss €36.4m (~$40m) vs €1.1m profit. Deal fees are 'one-off' only if the evoke deal stops generating them, which it will not until closing.

**Cash generation is the better story: 9M operating cash flow €206.6m (~$227m) vs €79.1m; Q3 OCF €73.2m (~$81m) vs €14.7m.** But 9M capex was €133.3m (~$147m), of which €85m (~$94m) was the 15-year Victoria (Australia) EGM-monitoring licence premium paid in Q2; underlying Q3 capex was ~€16m (~$17m, derived). OCF is stated before interest paid (IFRS financing classification), so after ~€100m+ of cash interest the 9M free cash flow is at best marginally positive.

**Leverage is the issue: adjusted net debt €1,629.9m (~$1.79bn), +€11m QoQ and +€136m YTD; pro-forma adjusted net leverage 4.33x vs 4.05x at Jun-26 and 3.5x at Dec-25/Mar-26.** Management stressed the QoQ move 'is arithmetic, not cash' — LTM PF AEBITDA fell to €376.7m from €399.9m — but the YTD net-debt increase is real: €85m Australia licence, €19.5m transaction/bond-issuance costs, €30.0m dividends and ~€21m of H1 buybacks. Funded debt rose to €1,882.0m (~$2.07bn) from €1,690.5m at Dec-25; total debt incl. leases ~€1.94bn (~$2.13bn).

**Covenant headroom is thin: the Intralot notes/RCF carry a total net leverage ceiling of 4.75x (per Bally's Corp 10-Q disclosure).** On our arithmetic, Q4-25 pro-forma AEBITDA was ~€103m (LTM €376.7m less 9M €273.6m); unless Q4-26 beats that pre-duty comparable, LTM AEBITDA falls further and Dec-26 leverage lands ~4.4-4.6x on flat-to-higher net debt (our estimate, see Forecast).

**Liquidity was rebuilt: €472.4m (~$520m) at 30 Sep vs €287.3m at 30 Jun, comprising €312.4m (~$344m) cash incl. restricted and a €160m (~$176m) undrawn RCF.** The driver was the £261.78m (~$340m) senior secured term facility signed 27 Jul, with £157.1m (~$204m; net £150.0m) drawn 30 Jul (matures Jul-2029, SONIA + 5.25-5.50%, bullet) and £104.7m undrawn. Cash and equivalents rose to €297.2m from €177.1m.

**evoke (William Hill/888) all-share acquisition — 0.537 new INLOT shares per evoke share, ~£243.1m (~$316m) equity value, 77% premium to the 17 Apr undisturbed price — approved by evoke shareholders on 18 Aug (99.63%) but completion now pushed to 2027.** The UKGC has confirmed evoke's licences continue on completion; remaining gating items are other gambling-regulator approvals and the Gibraltar court hearing. Management reiterated ~£180m (~$234m) of pre-tax cost and capex savings by the end of year two post-completion; the delay pushes that timetable out. Until closing the two groups are 'separate, independent and competing'.

**Parent-level overhang: Bally's Corp (NYSE: BALY) owns ~58% of Bally's Intralot and reports it as two segments — Bally's Intralot B2C revenue $257.5m (+22.8%) with Adj. EBITDAR $77.0m vs $86.4m (-10.9%), and B2B $76.6m vs $5.5m — combined $333.9m (+55%), EBITDAR $89.1m (-3%).** Bally's Corp has filed late 10-Qs for all three 2026 quarters, operates under a conditional RCF covenant waiver with a minimum-liquidity test (GamblingInsider reported on 17 Nov that the Q3 10-Q shows this requirement was missed — not verified by us against the filing), and held no Q3 call. The parent's funding needs are a structural risk to minority holders of INLOT.

**Capital allocation is mixed-signal: €30.0m (~$33m) of dividends and ~€21m (~$23m) of buybacks were paid in 9M while leverage rose above 4x; since 16 Jun a total-return equity swap with Deutsche Bank has seen DB buying INLOT shares weekly through November (synthetic buyback; terms not disclosed in sources read).** For a 4.3x-levered group with an acquisition pending, this is not what a deleveraging story looks like.

**B2B pipeline is a genuine offset to US weakness: 2026 wins include OLG (Ontario) selecting Intralot Canada as its lottery technology provider (Jun), Polla Chilena (Chile, Apr), the 15-year Victoria EGM-monitoring licence (Apr), BCLC shared services (Apr), the Hellenic Lotteries renewal with Allwyn Hellas (May) and the Premier Lotteries Ireland extension (Jul).** None is yet material to revenue; OLG conversion will be the swing factor for 2027-28 B2B.

**Pro-forma LTM: revenue €1,101.7m (~$1.21bn), AEBITDA €376.7m (~$414m), 34.2% margin.** The LTM margin is above the 33.0% 9M margin only because Q4-25 was pre-duty; the true run-rate margin for a 40%-RGD UK book is the 31% printed in Q2/Q3.

**Thesis read-through: the UK scale argument is holding — share gains as sub-scale rivals cut promotion (CBRE: 'scale is key') are visible in three quarters of accelerating cc growth at lower marketing cost.** But the equity is a levered option on (i) Q4 UK seasonality, (ii) a US jackpot cycle, (iii) evoke closing and the £180m synergy case being delivered on a target that itself was flagged as a going-concern risk. Shares -1.9% to ~€1.065 (~$1.17) on the 20 Nov full release (Investing.com; reaction on the 10 Nov preliminary not sourced).

segments.name: B2C – Bally's International Interactive (BII: UK, Spain, other online)
segments.headline: UK online +12.2% cc on lower marketing, record NGR for a third quarter; ~€34m/qtr RGD hit ~55% offset; segment margin stuck at ~31% post-duty vs ~39% pre-duty.
narrative: BII — the former Gamesys business (Jackpotjoy, Virgin Games, Monopoly Casino, Bally's-branded casino) acquired from Bally's Corp in October 2025 — is now the group: €201.6m (~$222m) of Q3 revenue, 70% of the total, up 4.0% quarter-on-quarter from ~€193.8m (~$213m). The UK is roughly 92% of the segment and ~65% of group revenue. UK online revenue rose 3.8% QoQ (+€6.8m, implying ~€185.7m (~$204m) in the quarter on our arithmetic) and 12.2% year-on-year in constant currency, the third successive acceleration (10.5% in Q1, 11.6% in Q2) and the third consecutive all-time-high quarterly net gaming revenue. Management was explicit that this was achieved on lower marketing investment than both the prior quarter and the prior year, and attributed it to organic growth and the strength of the installed player base rather than acquisition. They did not disclose actives, ARPU or marketing as a percentage of revenue, which is a disclosure gap for a business whose entire equity case rests on UK customer economics; the only colour was that Spain's growth came from a larger active base.

Spain delivered another record at €13.3m (~$15m), +18.9% YoY in constant currency and roughly +7% QoQ (Q2 was ~€12.4m after +15.1% YoY), again on more actives. The remaining ~€2-3m of BII revenue (other markets) is immaterial. Bally's Corp's USD view of the same business cross-checks: 'Bally's Intralot B2C' revenue of $257.5m, +22.8% YoY (this includes Bilyoner and Argentina), with segment Adjusted EBITDAR falling to $77.0m from $86.4m (-10.9%) — the cleanest single statement of what 40% RGD did to the UK book.

The profit picture is where the duty shows. We derive BII AEBITDA of ~€62.9m (~$69m) in Q3 (group €88.9m less legacy Intralot €26.0m), a ~31.2% margin, versus ~€60.1m / 31.0% in Q2 and ~€72.6m / 39.5% in Q1 before the duty change; the 9M figure of €195.6m (~$215m) (33.8%) was corroborated by Earnings+More. The RGD step-up from 21% to 40% on 1 April carried a gross negative AEBITDA impact of ~€34m (~$37m) in Q3, in line with Q2, for ~€68m (~$75m) year-to-date. Management says ~55% of the Q3 hit was offset year-on-year through top-line growth, marketing efficiency and disciplined cost management (Q2: 65%, which then comprised €11.3m of operating-cost optimisation and €10.1m of UK/Spain top-line growth). The 9M disclosure — gross-profit growth of €26.2m plus fixed-cost actions of €6.8m, i.e. €33.0m or ~49% of the €68m gross hit — does not reconcile to a 55-65% quarterly offset, so we treat the 'offset' ratio as a management construct rather than a hard bridge and use the 9M components. There is no separate cost-transformation programme with a named target; the offsets are run-rate marketing and overhead actions.

The structural read is that UK scale is working as the bull case predicted: with sub-scale operators pulling back promotion (first RGD receipts more than doubled to ~£590m, per NEXT.io's regulatory reporting) Bally's is taking share at lower cost per pound of NGR. The bear read is that the post-duty margin is now ~31% and will not recover towards the 35-39% of 2025 without pricing (lower RTP/bonusing) that would test the growth rate. Q2-27 is when the duty laps and reported UK growth stops being flattered by the 'through the duty' narrative; until then the right KPI is QoQ NGR. Segment guidance is qualitative only — continued UK growth, Spain records — and the evoke combination (William Hill, 888, Mr Green), slated for 2027, would roughly double the UK B2C footprint and bring the ~£180m (~$234m) two-year cost/capex synergy target into scope.

segments.name: Legacy Intralot – B2B lottery technology (US, RoW) and legacy B2C (Bilyoner Turkey, Argentina)
segments.headline: Stabilised QoQ (revenue +2.7%, AEBITDA +6.3% to €26.0m) on Bilyoner's seasonal rebound, but AEBITDA still -13% YoY as US lottery (-11% cc 9M) laps record jackpots and equipment sales.
narrative: The legacy Intralot perimeter — everything that was Intralot S.A. before the BII reverse-merger — generated €84.5m (~$93m) of Q3 revenue, up 2.7% QoQ and 3.2% above the €81.9m standalone Q3-25 base, and €26.0m (~$29m) of AEBITDA, up 6.3% QoQ but 13% below the €29.9m of a year ago; the margin was 30.8% against 36.5%. For nine months the perimeter did €251.1m (~$276m) of revenue (-4.9%) and €78.0m (~$86m) of AEBITDA (-13.4%). Management led the Q3 commentary with the sequential improvement, 'led by Bilyoner and Argentina'; the YoY decline, which is the more honest comparison for a business that did not change shape, was not emphasised.

B2B lottery is the drag. Nine-month revenue was €191.0m (~$210m), -8.1% reported and -6.2% in constant currency. The US — the largest market at €119.6m (~$132m) — was down 11% cc against a prior year boosted by record Powerball/Mega Millions jackpots and by equipment sales that did not recur; the rest of the portfolio (Greece, Australia, Ireland, Canada, LatAm, Africa) grew 3.6% cc. They continue to describe the US softness as 'softness and seasonality' and pointed in September to a stronger H2; Q3 did not obviously deliver that, and on our arithmetic B2B AEBITDA fell by several million euros QoQ since the legacy total rose only ~€1.5m while Bilyoner alone added €4.7m (~$5m). Bally's Corp's USD segment ('Bally's Intralot B2B') shows Q3 revenue of $76.6m, with implied EBITDAR of roughly $12m once the $77.0m B2C figure is deducted from the $89.1m combined total — a thin contribution for a business carrying the Intralot bond structure.

Legacy B2C is the bright spot. Bilyoner, the Turkish online sports betting operator, grew 20.6% in local currency for nine months but only 3.4% in euros to €45.8m (~$50m) — lira depreciation absorbs most of the growth — with amounts wagered up 28.4% versus a market up 17.8%, i.e. continued share gain. The business is highly seasonal around the Süper Lig: Q2 revenue fell 21.8% QoQ (-€3.6m) with a €3.2m AEBITDA drag, and Q3 recovered 25.8% QoQ (+€3.3m, to ~€16.1m (~$18m) on our estimate) with AEBITDA +€4.7m (~$5m). Argentina added €0.9m QoQ and is up 21.1% to €14.3m (~$16m) for nine months. Legacy B2C in total was €60.1m (~$66m), +7.1%. No actives, margins, or hold data are disclosed for either market.

The contract pipeline is the medium-term offset to US weakness and is genuinely better than a year ago: OLG (Ontario) selected Intralot Canada as its lottery technology provider in June; Polla Chilena de Beneficencia awarded a new contract in April; the 15-year Victoria EGM-monitoring licence (the €85m (~$94m) premium that inflated Q2 capex and net debt) was secured in April; BCLC shared services (April); the Hellenic Lotteries renewal with Allwyn Hellas (May); and the Premier Lotteries Ireland extension (July). None is yet in the numbers. There is no explicit segment guidance; the September call framed H2 as stronger in US lottery and Turkey, and the Q3 call split qualitative commentary between 'the BII business and the lotteries business' without numbers. Our read is that B2B revenue will track the jackpot cycle and the timing of OLG/Chile hardware, and that the Bilyoner Q4 (football season) is the more predictable earnings lift.

highlights.text: UK online NGR +12.2% YoY cc in Q3, accelerating for a third quarter (10.5% → 11.6% → 12.2%) and a third straight all-time high, achieved on lower marketing — the scale/share-gain thesis under 40% RGD is being evidenced, not asserted.
Group AEBITDA +5.1% QoQ to €88.9m (~$98m) with margin +50bps to 31.1%, despite a flat ~€34m (~$37m) quarterly duty burden; the post-duty margin floor appears to be ~31%.

Liquidity rebuilt to €472.4m (~$520m) from €287.3m via the £261.78m (~$340m) 2029 term facility (£104.7m still undrawn); operating cash flow of €73.2m (~$81m) in Q3 and €206.6m (~$227m) for 9M is real cash before interest.
Bilyoner rebounded 25.8% QoQ in revenue and added €4.7m (~$5m) of AEBITDA, with wagers growing 28.4% vs a market at 17.8%; legacy Intralot AEBITDA +6.3% QoQ.

B2B pipeline refreshed (OLG Ontario, Polla Chilena, Victoria 15-year monitoring, BCLC, Hellenic Lotteries, PLI Ireland) — not in the numbers yet, but the first positive contract momentum in several years.

lowlights.text: Pro-forma adjusted net leverage 4.33x vs 4.05x at Jun-26 and 3.5x at Dec-25, against a 4.75x total net leverage covenant; LTM PF AEBITDA has fallen €54m (~$59m) in nine months to €376.7m (~$414m) and will fall further in Q4 unless the quarter beats the ~€103m pre-duty Q4-25 comparable (our arithmetic).

Net loss after tax €23.8m (~$26m) in Q3 and €36.4m (~$40m) for 9M; net finance costs €109.7m (~$121m) YTD and €27.7m (~$30m) of transaction fees — the capital structure consumes ~40% of AEBITDA before any deleveraging.

US lottery revenue -11% cc for 9M (€119.6m / ~$132m) on jackpot and equipment comps; legacy Intralot AEBITDA -13% YoY in Q3 and -13.4% for 9M. The 'stronger H2' promised in September is not yet visible.

evoke completion slipped to 2027 (Gibraltar court, further regulator approvals), deferring the ~£180m (~$234m) synergy clock and extending the period in which deal fees accrue and the target — which flagged going-concern uncertainty tied to Bally's intentions — operates independently.

Parent Bally's Corp (58% holder) has filed three late 10-Qs in 2026, operates under a covenant waiver with a minimum-liquidity test (reported missed per GamblingInsider, unverified by us), and held no Q3 call; the parent's funding needs are a governance and capital-allocation overhang on INLOT minorities.

Disclosure is thin for a B2C-led group: no actives, ARPU, marketing % of revenue, hold or segment EBITDA by quarter; the duty 'offset' metric moves between 49% (9M components), 55% (Q3) and 65% (Q2) without a consistent definition.

€30m (~$33m) of dividends, ~€21m (~$23m) of H1 buybacks and an ongoing Deutsche Bank total-return-swap purchase programme while leverage rose through 4x — capital allocation is at odds with the deleveraging the covenant requires.

forecast.intro: Bally's Intralot does not publish numeric group guidance, so there is no 'old vs new' to reconcile; the operative forward-looking numbers are the LTM pro-forma AEBITDA that sets covenant leverage and management's qualitative steer (continued UK online growth; stronger H2 in US lottery and Turkey; evoke closing in 2027, Earnings+More cites January). The division driving the deterioration in the leverage denominator is BII (UK duty, ~€34m/qtr gross, roughly half recovered), with legacy B2B (US lottery) the secondary drag; the division driving the sequential improvement is also BII (UK NGR +3.8% QoQ) plus Bilyoner's seasonal recovery. The bridge below walks LTM PF AEBITDA from Dec-25 to Sep-26; the split beyond the first line is our estimate.

forecast.view: **Q4-26e (our estimate): revenue €290-300m (~$319-330m), AEBITDA €88-95m (~$97-105m), margin ~30-32%.** The UK bingo/casino book is seasonally strongest in Q4 and the Süper Lig lifts Bilyoner, but the duty is now fully in the base and the US needs a jackpot run to lap a strong Q4-25. That puts **FY26e revenue at ~€1.12-1.13bn (~$1.23-1.24bn) and AEBITDA at ~€362-369m (~$398-406m), a ~32% margin** — below the €376.7m LTM print, because Q4-25 PF AEBITDA (~€103m) was pre-duty. **Leverage therefore rises again at Dec-26: on flat net debt of ~€1.63bn we get ~4.4-4.5x; with the October bond coupon and any further DB share purchases pushing net debt to ~€1.66bn, ~4.5-4.6x — inside the 4.75x ceiling but with headroom of only ~€10-20m of AEBITDA.** The direction only reverses in H2-27 when the duty laps (Q2-27), OLG/Chile revenue starts, and — if it closes — evoke's EBITDA enters the denominator; but evoke brings its own debt and a 'material uncertainty' balance sheet, so pro-forma leverage is more likely to rise than fall at completion before the £180m synergies land in 2028-29. Net: revenue up, margin flat at ~31%, leverage up through year-end; the equity is a call on execution in 2027, not on 2026 numbers.
watch: Q4 UK NGR growth (cc) vs the ~€34m quarterly duty: anything below ~10% cc suggests the share-gain tailwind is fading before the Q2-27 lap.
Dec-26 pro-forma leverage vs the 4.75x covenant: watch Q4 AEBITDA against the ~€103m Q4-25 PF comparable and any further Deutsche Bank TRS purchases or dividend declarations that add to net debt.
evoke closing timetable: remaining gambling-regulator approvals and the Gibraltar court hearing (company: 2027; E+M: January 2027), plus evoke's own Q4 trading and going-concern language.
US lottery: jackpot cycle, equipment-sales timing and OLG (Ontario) contract conversion into 2027 revenue; legacy B2B AEBITDA needs to stop falling YoY.
Bilyoner: Q4 football-season revenue and TRY/EUR — 20.6% local-currency growth became 3.4% in euros for 9M.
Parent Bally's Corp: 10-Q timeliness, RCF covenant waiver/minimum-liquidity compliance, going-concern language and any upstreaming or asset moves that affect INLOT minorities.
UK regulation: Gambling Act review implementation (affordability checks, bonus restrictions) and whether a second-round RGD or stake-limit change appears in the 2027 fiscal calendar.
Disclosure: whether the FY25/FY26 annual report finally gives actives, ARPU and marketing % of revenue for the UK book — without them the 'marketing efficiency' claim cannot be audited.
